chunks: And whatever in this book is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Halabi, I have transmitted it from my father; and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan; and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with them - from Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Halabi.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to the author's father)
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: May Allah be pleased with them
key_terms.صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى: Safwan ibn Yahya, a prominent narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْحَلَبِيُّ: Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Halabi, a key narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Halabi's narrations verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a detailed isnad verification for narrations from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, tracing the chain through his father, al-Saduq, and other key Tabi'un and Imami scholars like Abd Allah ibn Maskan and Safwan ibn Yahya. This emphasis on a robust, multi-generational chain underscores the reliability of the transmission within the Shia scholarly tradition, ensuring the authenticity of the reported teachings.
